                    How to Register to Vote        
A person must meet the following to register and vote in New Hampshire: 
Photo ID              
18 years of age or older on election day.              
A United States citizen.              
Domiciled in the town or ward where the person seeks to vote.              
Registering to Vote in New Hampshire   (See: Documents)  – provides further details on these requirements. 
Where To Register to Vote         
A person can register to vote: 
Town Clerk’s Office 
Address – 143 Main St, Belmont 
Hours – Monday – Friday 7:30am – 4:00pm 
Supervisors of the Checklist Meeting 
Where – Belmont Town Hall, 143 Main St, Belmont 
At the Polling Place  
Where – Belmont High School, 255 Seavey Rd, Belmont  
When- November 3, 2026 from 7:00am to 7:00pm  
Absentee by Mail 
Voters who are unable to register in person because of physical disability, religious reasons, military service or absence from town, may register by mail. 
Request an absentee voter registration packet from the town clerk.  
The absentee voter registration form must be witnessed by another person. Both forms are to be returned to the town clerk. 
                    How To Vote        
Vote in Person 
Polling Location: 
255 Seavey Road, Belmont, NH 
Polling Hours: 
7:00 AM – 7:00 PM 
Bring a Photo ID 
A valid photo ID is required to receive a ballot. 
Need Assistance? 
Accessible voting information is available at: 
https://www.sos.nh.gov/elections/voting-disabilities 
Vote by Absentee Ballot 
Any registered New Hampshire voter may request an absentee ballot for the 2026 Primary Election. 
To request a ballot, submit a signed absentee ballot application to the Belmont Town Clerk in person, by mail, fax, or email at tctc@belmontnh.gov. A separate application is required for each election and must include a handwritten signature. 
You must verify your identity by one of the following: 
Including a copy of a valid photo ID. 
Having your application notarized. 
Presenting your photo ID to the Town Clerk before your ballot is issued. 
Once your application is approved, you may: 
Vote your ballot at Town Hall and return it immediately. 
Take your ballot home and return it to Town Hall during regular business hours or by mail. 
Have your ballot mailed to you and return it according to the enclosed instructions. 
Absentee ballots will only be issued to the voter requesting the ballot. 
Applications are available at the Belmont Town Clerk’s Office, on the Town website at belmontnh.gov, or from the New Hampshire Secretary of State at  www.sos.nh.gov/elections/voters . 
Voters living outside the United States may use the UOCAVA absentee ballot application. 
For questions, contact the Belmont Town Clerk’s Office at (603) 267-8300, Ext. 2. 
                    Voting Statistics        
As of July 14, 2026, there are: 
4,522 Voters  Registered in the Town of Belmont: 
Democrats – 974 
Republicans – 2,165 
Undeclared – 1,383 
Libertarian – 0
